# Monaka contract C2 — wire 2.0

This coordinated Architecture Revision supersedes C1's capability and namespace semantics. C1 remains the historical wire 1.0 specification. JSON framing, limits, clocks, units, Hamilton xyzw, coordinates, strict validation, message types, ports and division of responsibilities otherwise remain as in C1.

All four messages require `version.major=2`, `version.minor=0` and `modality`: `full`, `rotation_only`, or `none`. Pose FULL guarantees both valid components; ROTATION_ONLY guarantees orientation only (position validity must be false); NONE permits neither valid component. Numeric invalid fields are diagnostic only. The codec rejects inconsistent validity. State modality is informational and cannot create, repair, upgrade, or refresh a pose. Inactive tracking_state/presence must use none. Evidence is independent of modality. Unsupported vendor loss semantics fail closed to none; no synthetic IMU stream may be derived from a FULL sample.

MTP requires `publisher_id`, the persistent Bridge installation identity. `source_id` preserves the backend installation identity. Runtime lifetime identity is `(publisher_id,source_id)`, tracker identity is `(publisher_id,source_id,tracker_id)`. Session/clock belong to the Bridge publisher lifetime; input source/device/session/sequence belong to the upstream backend sample. MtpPose.input additionally requires `source_id` and `orientation_evidence` (C1 evidence values). input.source_id must equal source_id. A tracker name may recur across sources or publishers. Modality, body assignment, mapping revision, UDP ports, and session never enter persistent identity.

Battery timestamp uses the envelope clock and must be no later than sent_at_ns. Consumers reject negative or unrepresentable age before subtraction. An absent/lost/disconnected state establishes a session-local timestamp watermark. Present metadata never revives a sample. A strictly newer pose may recover even if a present notification was lost; poses at or before the watermark are rejected. Duplicate/reordered poses never refresh age.

A different peer/session cannot take over an active source lease. A competing packet is rejected without permanently poisoning the source or refreshing its lease. After 500 ms without accepted traffic (or the configured lease), a new session can replace it and retires the old session. Same-session peer changes and conflicting duplicate samples are rejected; peer is not persistent identity. Continuous competing processes do not receive simultaneous ownership. Restart recovery is bounded by lease expiry, not immediate unconditional UUID takeover.

Main/Fallback policy and body targets remain local to MonakaVR. Main FULL and usable owns both components. Otherwise position is unavailable; explicitly assigned usable fallback orientation is preferred, then usable Main rotation, else neither. Unknown/PRECISION external semantics fail closed. Config migration preserves unambiguous existing trackers as Main and leaves fallback empty.

Version 1 packets are rejected by v2 runtime codecs; v1 consumers likewise reject v2. No runtime auto-upgrade by inferring modality from stale numeric fields. All publishers/consumers must be upgraded together using the same actual kit. Existing v1 artifacts are retained unchanged and cannot serve as v2 acceptance evidence.
